rows.grounds: compound: artha-sāmarthya-ja (born from the capacity/power of the object); qualifies jñānaṃ
subject of matam; cognition arising from the object's capacity
compound: smṛti-saṅkalpa-vat (possessing the nature of memory and conception); indicates epistemic status
past passive participle expressing the accepted view

items.question: What is the epistemic status of cognition born from an object's own capacity?
premises: Cognition can arise from the capacity of the object itself.
Such cognition is comparable to memory and conception.
Memory and conception are not instances of direct perception.
items.inference: Therefore, cognition born from an object's capacity is not established as direct perception but is regarded as akin to memory and conception.
uncertainties: The precise distinction intended between smṛti and saṅkalpa in this context is not fully specified.
items.plain_english: Cognition that arises from the capacity of the object is considered to be like memory and conceptual construction.
